name: Miyoo Mini

models.name: Mini v1–4
models.notes: Grouped by spruceOS as 'Mini v1-4'; four model revisions share the same form factor and hardware

summary: Miyoo's pocket-sized handheld. spruceOS groups Mini revisions v1–4 under a single supported entry with 'Stable' status. No KNULLI image available. Hardware specifications not sourced from verified vendor or community pages at the time of check (2026-10-28).

variants.notes: Pocket-sized Miyoo device. spruceOS groups Mini revisions v1–4 under one supported entry ('Stable'). spruceOS lists the Miyoo Mini Plus as a separate Stable entry from Mini v1-4; Onion's installation page covers both Mini (MM) and Mini+ (MMP) and calls Onion a frontend on the SD card, with the firmware as the backend inside the device. This record covers Mini v1-4 only. Four documented model revisions share the same form factor. No KNULLI image available (checked KNULLI Scarab 2026-05-11 releases). Hardware specifications not sourced from verified vendor or community pages at the time of check.

homebrew.name: spruceOS
homebrew.firmware: Custom Python-based frontend on top of the Miyoo stock OS.
homebrew.summary: Custom frontend that runs on top of the stock OS on supported Miyoo devices.

compatibility.note: spruceOS lists 'Miyoo Mini v1-4' with 'Stable' support status (checked 2026-10-28).

requirements: A new branded microSD card (do NOT use the stock card).
warnings: spruceOS is a frontend, not a full OS replacement; it runs on top of the stock OS.
spruceOS groups Mini revisions v1–4 as a single entry; hardware differences between revisions are undocumented.

homebrew.name: OnionOS
homebrew.firmware: Frontend on the SD card, not a firmware replacement: Onion's installation page calls the firmware the backend inside the device. Requires stock firmware 20220419**** or newer (for Onion v3.10 and above).
homebrew.summary: Community frontend for the Miyoo Mini that runs from the SD card on top of the stock firmware.

compatibility.note: Onion's installation page names the Miyoo Mini (MM) and requires at least firmware 20220419**** for Onion v3.10 and above. The page gives example versions, not an exhaustive tested matrix, so no exact firmware list is claimed here; it marks 20231027 as only for MM v4.

requirements: A Miyoo Mini (MM) with stock firmware 20220419**** or newer.
A branded SD card formatted FAT32, not exFAT.
The Onion release zip extracted, with its folders copied to the SD card root.
warnings: Onion is a frontend, not a full OS replacement; it runs on the stock firmware, which must already meet the minimum version.
Devices on firmware 20221216**** or 20221224**** ('The Boya Incident') need the community patch first.
The SD card included with the Miyoo Mini is known to be slow and can ruin the experience or data; use a reputable brand.

homebrew.name: Koriki
homebrew.firmware: SD-card software compilation that runs over the stock firmware; release v1.7.0 states compatibility with Miyoo Mini v1, v2, v3 and v4.
homebrew.summary: SimpleMenu-based software compilation installed on the microSD card over the stock firmware.

compatibility.note: Koriki's README says it runs over stock firmware; its v1.7.0 release notes list the Miyoo Mini v1, v2, v3 and v4 as compatible, with one card auto-detecting the model.

requirements: A Miyoo Mini v1, v2, v3 or v4.
A microSD card formatted FAT32 with 32K clusters.
For a new install: Koriki_vx.x.x.img.gz written with balenaEtcher or Rufus, or Koriki_vx.x.x_full.zip unzipped to the card root.
warnings: Koriki runs over the stock firmware rather than replacing it.

homebrew.name: MinUI
homebrew.firmware: Custom launcher and libretro frontend on a single SD card; the supported-devices table lists Miyoo Mini with Legacy status.
homebrew.summary: Minimal launcher and libretro frontend distributed for a single SD card across several handhelds.

compatibility.note: MinUI's supported-devices table lists Miyoo Mini (added MinUI-20230922b-2) with Legacy status, which the page defines as 'will be retired in a future update'.

requirements: A Miyoo Mini listed in MinUI's supported-devices table.
A microSD card; MinUI describes one card compatible with multiple listed devices.
warnings: MinUI marks Miyoo Mini as Legacy; the page says Legacy devices will be retired in a future update.
MinUI describes itself as a launcher and libretro frontend, not a full OS image.
